title: The Kunneth map
statement:
Let $X,Y,S$ be schemes and let
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
Z=X\times_SY&\xrightarrow{\;q\;}&Y\\
p\downarrow&&\downarrow g\\
X&\xrightarrow{\;f\;}&S
\end{array}
$$
be a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], with $c=f\circ p=g\circ q$. Fix a commutative ring $\Lambda$. Work on small representatives of the small etale sites in a universe large enough for the module sheaves [def-weil-size-convention], with the unbounded categories $D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. All tensor products below are the ordinary uncompleted derived tensor product [def-kun-derived-tensor], acting on pairs of morphisms through the bifunctor of [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent].

For every scheme morphism $u:U\to V$ in the diagram, use the inverse image of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] on constant-coefficient module sheaves. It is additive, exact and left adjoint to $u_*$ [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Denote its termwise descent to the unbounded derived categories again by $u^{-1}$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. For a representing complex $C$ and a K-injective resolution $C\to I$ [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist], use $Ru_*(QC)=Q(u_*I)$, the total right derived functor supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. Use the canonical adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv Ru_*$, with unit $\eta_u$ and counit $\varepsilon_u$. Its Hom bijection is the composite
$$
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(U_{\Et},\Lambda)}(u^{-1}QM,QI)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(U_{\Et},\Lambda)}(u^{-1}M,I)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(V_{\Et},\Lambda)}(M,u_*I)
\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(V_{\Et},\Lambda)}(QM,Q(u_*I)),
$$
where $K(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$ denotes the category of cochain complexes modulo chain homotopy. These are the K-injective Hom bijections [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] and the termwise adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]; $u_*I$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], since its left adjoint is exact.

Use the canonical composition identifications
$$
\gamma_{f,p}:c^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}p^{-1}f^{-1},\qquad
\gamma_{g,q}:c^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}q^{-1}g^{-1}.
$$
They are the inverses of the sheaf composition isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], with their canonical constant-coefficient module lifts supplied by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition-module-linear], then applied termwise and descended by clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. The cited module-linearity lemma states that these very sheaf composition maps respect the module actions of [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] and the composite-adjunction units. Naturality also makes them commute with the differentials of complexes; exactness makes both composite functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Thus this construction uses unbounded module categories, without invoking a bounded-below composition assertion.

Let $E\in D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ and $K\in D(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$, and put
$$
A=Rf_*E\kunotimes{\Lambda}Rg_*K,\qquad
B=p^{-1}E\kunotimes{\Lambda}q^{-1}K.
$$
Write $\mu^c_{L,M}:c^{-1}L\kunotimes{\Lambda}c^{-1}M\xrightarrow{\sim}c^{-1}(L\kunotimes{\Lambda}M)$ for the canonical comparison of [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal]. Define $\alpha_{E,K}:c^{-1}A\to B$ to be the composite
$$
\begin{aligned}
c^{-1}A
&\xrightarrow{(\mu^c_{Rf_*E,Rg_*K})^{-1}}
c^{-1}Rf_*E\kunotimes{\Lambda}c^{-1}Rg_*K\\
&\xrightarrow{\gamma_{f,p,Rf_*E}\kunotimes{\Lambda}\gamma_{g,q,Rg_*K}}
p^{-1}f^{-1}Rf_*E\kunotimes{\Lambda}q^{-1}g^{-1}Rg_*K\\
&\xrightarrow{p^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,E})\kunotimes{\Lambda}q^{-1}(\varepsilon_{g,K})}
p^{-1}E\kunotimes{\Lambda}q^{-1}K=B.
\end{aligned}
$$
The *Kunneth map* (or *external product map*) is the morphism in $D(S_{\Et},\Lambda)$ defined by
$$
\kappa_{E,K}: A\xrightarrow{\eta_{c,A}}Rc_*c^{-1}A
\xrightarrow{Rc_*(\alpha_{E,K})}Rc_*B.
$$
Equivalently, it is the morphism adjoint to $\alpha_{E,K}$ under $c^{-1}\dashv Rc_*$. This definition imposes no boundedness, properness, finite-type or torsion assumption and includes no assertion that $\kappa_{E,K}$ is an isomorphism.
